Their EO components and polyphenols possess a wide range of biological activities, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytotoxic effects (Kindl et al., 2019; Li et al., 2019). Scientific research revealed various biological properties related to the content of EO (citral, nerol, geraniol, citronellal, terpinolene) and polyphenols (luteolin and its 6-C and 7-O–glycosides, isoorientin 2′-O-rhamnoside, quercetin, kaempferol, apigenin, elimicin, catecol, chlorogenic acid and caffeic acid and hydroquinone) in the leaves, such as antimicrobial, anthelmintic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antiproliferative, antidiabetic and antihyperlipidemic activities (Majewska et al., 2019; Mukarram et al., 2022; Shah et al., 2011). The largest and the most studied group of natural antioxidants are plant polyphenols that can be classified as flavonoids and non‐flavonoids (phenolic acids, tannins, stilbenes, lignans and other phenols) (Luo et al., 2021). The main bioactive constituents of this plant are phenolic acids, such as caffeic and rosmarinic acids and different types of flavonoids, such as luteolin, apigenin and hesperetin (Schuhmacher et al., 2003).

Chlorogenic Acid, Quercetin-3-Rutinoside and Black Tea Phenols Are Extensively Metabolized in Humans. Chlorogenic Acid, Quercetin-3-Rutinoside and Black Tea Phenols Are Extensively Metabolized in Humans. The aim of this study was to identify and quantify the phenolic acid metabolites of chlorogenic acid (major phenol in coffee), quercetin-3-rutinoside (major flavonol in tea) and black tea phenols in humans, and determine the site of metabolism. Healthy humans (n = 20) with an intact colon participated in a dietary controlled crossover study, and we identified and quantified ∼60 potential phenolic acid metabolites in urine. Half of the ingested chlorogenic acid and 43% of the tea phenols were metabolized to hippuric acid. In contrast, in seven humans without a colon, we found only traces of phenolic acid metabolites in urine after they had ingested chlorogenic acid and quercetin-3-rutinoside.
